title: Lower-limb anthropometry adds modest transported information about elevated glycated hemoglobin beyond BMI and waist circumference
abstract: Primary studies suggest that thigh size carries metabolic information beyond central adiposity. We tested frozen model transport from NHANES III (1988–1994; n=13781) to separately recruited NHANES 1999–2000 (n=3524). For biochemical glycated hemoglobin ≥5.7%, adding waist-to-thigh ratio to weighted logistic models with flexible age, BMI, waist, height, sex and ethnicity reduced target weighted Brier score from 0.116400 to 0.113318; delta -0.003082, joint stratified-PSU bootstrap95% interval [-0.004745,-0.001295]. AUC changed by +0.007311. Adding the ratio after flexible thigh circumference gave only -0.000006 further Brier change, suggesting lower-limb information rather than a uniquely useful ratio. This exploratory cross-sectional temporal transport is not a new biomarker discovery, causal inference, incident-diabetes prediction, or clinical validation.
